Identification_Area.title: (99942) Apophis pole orientation and rotation period

Observing_System_Component.name: DSS-14 X-band Goldstone Solar System Radar Transmitter
DSS-14 X-band Goldstone Solar System Radar Receiver

External_Reference.reference_text: Brozovic, M., Benner, L., McMichael, J., Giorgini, J., Pravec, P., Scheirich, P., Magri, M., Busch, M., Jao, J., Lee. C., Snedecker, L., Silva, M., Slade, M., Semenov, B., Nolan, M., Taylor, P., Howell, E., Lawrence, K., Icarus 300, 115-128, 2018, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2017.08.032.
External_Reference.description: This data set contains a preliminary three-dimensional shape model and rotation state of near-Earth asteroid (99942) Apophis based on ground-based radar images as reported by Brozovic et al. (2018). The rotation state is the same as Model R in the Supplementary Table 1 in Brozovic et al. 2018. The spin state is listed in the Pravec et al. 2014 notation for non-principal axis rotation.

Field_Delimited.name: Rotational_period1, P(phi)
Field_Delimited.description: Period of the asteroid's Euler angle, P(phi) or P1. The period of the precession of the short axis around the angular momentum vector. The Samarasinha convention is used (Samarasinha and A'Hearn, 1991).

Field_Delimited.name: Rotational_period1_error
Field_Delimited.description: Uncertainty of the rotational period, P(phi) or P1

Field_Delimited.name: Rotational_period2, P(psi)
Field_Delimited.description: Period of the asteroid's Euler angle, P(psi) or P2. The period of rotation of the body around short principal axis. The units of P2 is hours. Within the Supplementary Table 1 in Brozovic et al. 2018 the units are stated as days which is incorrect. The Samarasinha convention is used (Samarasinha and A'Hearn, 1991).

Field_Delimited.name: Rotational_period2_error
Field_Delimited.description: Uncertainty of the rotational period, P(psi) or P2

Field_Delimited.name: Euler_angle_of_rotation_at_t0_year

Field_Delimited.description: Moment of inertia ratio, Ii/Is, for the intermediate and short axes of the body's ellipsoid of inertia
